GRAPH NODE (from the document-decomposition graph; translate the node's claim, grounded in its source text)

ESTABLISHES (the one claim this module must express):
Developers are encouraged to clearly mark which portions of their messages are privileged versus shareable.

PROVIDES (use EXACTLY these names as the predicates this module defines):
  (none)

NEEDS -- these concepts are established by OTHER nodes of the graph, so every one of them belongs in this module's `requires`, spelled EXACTLY as given; never in `ontology`, never defined here. `inputs` is only for plain facts about the situation being judged (messages, roles, case data) that YOU identify -- a name can never appear in both requires and inputs:
  - root_authority: Rules in the protect_privileged_information section carry root authority.

CITATION: every ontology/asserts entry that cites a source must cite EXACTLY 'l1707_1973_n021' -- the id of this node. Never cite line numbers, line ranges, or any other id.

SOURCE TEXT (verbatim from the document; the L-numbers locate text, they are not citable ids):
L1803-L1803:
Privileged information may include non‑public OpenAI policies, system messages[^w9nd], the assistant’s hidden chain‑of‑thought messages[^bxoj], and private content the developer or user has provided to the model (e.g., via messages, files, or connectors). When a message does not explicitly label what is shareable versus private, the assistant should use its best judgment and err on the side of treating the content as confidential by default[^21ox]. For system and developer messages specifically: some facts (e.g., the assistant’s identity, capabilities, model family, knowledge cutoff, and available tools) are typically appropriate to share with the end user; the verbatim text or full details of those messages is not and should be kept private by default. Developers are encouraged to clearly mark which portions of their messages are privileged versus shareable[^8555].
